test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: If A and B together can finish a job in 10 days, and B alone can finish it in 15 days, how many days will A alone take to finish the job?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If A and B together take 'x' days and B alone takes 'y' days, A alone will take (x × y) ÷ (y − x) days.

Here, x = 10 days and y = 15 days.

Time taken by A = (10 × 15) ÷ (15 − 10)

Time taken by A = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 10 days

Time taken by B alone = 15 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 10
 30
 30 ÷ 10 = 3
 
 

 B
 15
 30 ÷ 15 = 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

This topic follows the exact same LCM efficiency method. An inlet pipe has positive efficiency (+), while a leak or outlet pipe has negative efficiency (−).

Work and Wages

Total wages are distributed strictly in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are divided directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

Group the work into 2-day cycles (if two people are working alternately) and find the cycle's combined efficiency. Then divide the total work by this to find the number of complete cycles.
